home.whatYouGet: It's not a guess. It's a calculation report.
home.whatYouGetSubtitle: The store salesman calculates BTU by square meter. The standard considers solar orientation, ceiling height, glazing, occupancy and equipment. The difference shows up in your electric bill every month — and in the compressor that dies early.
home.deliverable1: Calculation per the applicable standard (ABNT, ASHRAE, ISO)
home.deliverable2: Open calculation memory — you see where every number came from
home.deliverable3: Equipment suggested by model, not by "more or less this"
home.deliverable4: Estimated consumption and what the installer must meet
home.reportFooter: Calculation by square meter would suggest 9,000 BTU/h in this room. The west orientation and glazing area change the result — and an undersized unit runs at the limit all day.

home.faqTitle: Questions from those just getting started.
home.faq1Q: Do I need a site visit?
home.faq1A: In most residential cases, no. You provide the measurements and send photos via WhatsApp — that's usually enough for sizing. When the case requires an on-site inspection (existing structure report, for example), I'll tell you before any charge.
home.faq2A: Each case is quoted individually based on scope, timeline and applicable standard. You get the price before any commitment and only pay after approving delivery. Simple sizing services cost well below what a site visit usually costs.
home.faq3A: Yes, on demand. ART doesn't come built into the standard price because most residential services don't require registration — charging everyone for something only some need would increase costs unnecessarily. When your case requires it, the price is quoted separately.
home.faq4A: Yes. Calculation is adapted to the standard of the requesting country — ASHRAE, ISO, Eurocode, AISC, ASME, among others. Service is available in Portuguese, English or written Spanish.
home.faq5Q: How long until I get it?
home.faq5A: Simple sizing: 24 to 48 hours. Reports and structural verification: 3 to 10 days, depending on survey needs. Full projects have a deadline in the proposal. If you're in a rush, let me know — there's an expedited option.
home.faq6Q: What if the report doesn't solve my problem?
home.faq6A: You don't pay. Payment happens after your approval, not before. Every delivery includes two rounds of revision at no cost — if something was imprecise or missing, it gets corrected.
home.heroLedeNote: *Turnaround depends on current demand and is agreed when the service is contracted.

work.metaDescription: Mining, energy, healthcare and building services: selected structural, HVAC, pumping and mechanical projects delivered over the past fifteen years.
work.heroLede: Mining, energy, rail, healthcare and building services. A selection of projects delivered over the past fifteen years — structural analysis, HVAC, pumping, mechanical design and field inspection. It is the same engineering that answers when you ask which air conditioner to buy.
work.heroNote: Every image comes from a delivered project. Client identification and contractual data have been removed from the drawings.
work.pumpingBody: From abrasive slurry in a tailings basin to the cold water main of a building, the maths is the same: flow, head, NPSH and the pump's real curve.
work.tailingsBody: Slurry discharge system: pump selection, pipe routing and NPSH check with the abrasive wear of the material accounted for.
work.boostingBody: Building booster set modelled in BIM — head, pump curve and pipe supports all come out of the same model, with no surprises during installation.
work.structuralBody: A whole portal frame or a single weld: the criterion does not change. Load combinations, code checks and, where the case calls for it, finite element analysis.
work.shedBody: Frames, bracing and connections checked against load combinations. The map shows displacements up to 11.6 mm and a utilisation ratio U = 0.88 at the critical connections.
work.fopsBody: Virtual test to ISO 3449: impact simulated by finite elements on the cab, with a maximum total deformation of 7.52 mm at the roof.
work.lugBody: Von Mises stress on the lug and its reinforcement plate — a 142.7 MPa peak, with a stated margin over the yield strength of the specified steel.
work.towerBody: Structural design of the tower and its movable maintenance platform — from the 3D model to the assembled unit in the field, with the operator on board.
work.hvacBody: Cooling load calculated per space, not per square metre. A factory canteen, an electrical substation and an office each demand a different answer.
work.canteenBody: Cooling load with occupancy and kitchen combined, equipment selection and condenser placement coordinated with the architecture and with maintenance access.
work.ductsBody: Duct routing, flexible connections and diffusers coordinated with the roof structure — the clash shows up in the model, not on site.
work.substationBody: A space whose cooling load is dominated by equipment: supply, return and redundancy sized for continuous operation, with no planned shutdown.
work.mechanicalBody: Equipment drawn to be manufactured: drive, geometry, sealing and detailing at the level the fabrication shop needs to start cutting plate.
work.conveyorBody: Mechanical design of the conveyor, its drive and the transfer chute geometry — detailing delivered ready for fabrication.
work.gatesBody: Mechanical and process design of the gates: actuation, sealing and structure sized for the water column and the operating regime.
work.fieldBody: A design never verified in the field is only a drawing. Manufacturing follow-up, acceptance testing and utility networks with codes of their own.
work.valvesBody: Incoming inspection of hydraulic valves: runout and flange flatness measured with a dial indicator before the equipment ships to site.
work.gasesBody: Detailed design of the plant room and the distribution of oxygen, compressed air and nitrous oxide: cylinder shelter, outlet stations, alarm panel and bill of materials.

work.closingTitle: Your problem is probably smaller than these. The maths is the same.
work.closingBody: The criterion that sizes the air conditioning of a substation is the one that sizes the unit in your bedroom: the applicable code, the real load and equipment chosen by number, not by guesswork. Describe what you need and I reply within 24 hours.
